column1: # Model compounds for the direction substitution lane.
# Every structure here is COPIED BY MACHINE from MetaNetX 4.5 chem_prop, keyed on
# `source_mnxm`; nothing in this file is hand-transcribed. The curation is which concrete
# compound stands in for which generic carrier, and that lives in substitutions.tsv --
# this file only says what those compounds are.
# `congener_of` names the model this one is a defensible alternative to. `substitute
# anchor` scores the anchor reaction under each and reports the spread, which becomes the
# row's sigma_sub: the width of the curator's choice, carried rather than discarded.
# `formula` is read only by the POLYMER scope, which decides per reaction whether inserting
# the acceptor closes the equation's heavy-atom deficit. It is chem_prop's own string and
# `_admit_models` refuses any row whose formula disagrees with its `source_mnxm`.
# EVERY MODEL COMPOUND MUST RESOLVE IN eQUILIBRATOR'S FROZEN CACHE, and the oxidised half
# is where that fails. MetaNetX carries FMN twice -- MNXM1364147 at charge 0 and MNXM1364148
# at -3 -- and eQuilibrator knows only the second; FAD has no resolving accession at all,
# which is why the flavin congener here is riboflavin and not FAD. `substitute anchor
# --member eq` reports this as `member_silent`/`unresolved`, per compound. Check a new model
# there before trusting it: a compound that does not resolve silences the whole reaction it
# A `#` is a comment ONLY at line start -- SMILES carry `#` triple bonds.
# THE ACYL-CARRIER MODELS. ACP presents its acyl group on 4'-phosphopantetheine, so the
# model is that arm itself and the thioester is bonded to the same atoms it is bonded to
# in vivo -- the protein sits a phosphoester away and carries no term either member reads.
# The acyl-CoA of the same acyl group is declared as its CONGENER: the second backbone a
# curator could defensibly have chosen, so the choice carries a width instead of implying
# none. Every structure here is chem_prop's own, copied by machine; none is constructed.
